data.long_meaning: The name Mathew is derived from the Hebrew name Mattityahu, which means 'gift of God'. In the New Testament, Mathew is one of the twelve apostles, also known as Levi before his conversion. The name Mathew carries the meaning “Gift of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Mathew usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mathew is popular in many cultures, most notably in Christian communities. It is a common name in both the United States and the United Kingdom. In the Middle Ages, Matthew was a popular name for knights and warriors, reflecting the biblical character's role as a disciple and later a tax collector for the Roman Empire. The name is also associated with mathematics due to the belief that Mathew was the author of the first gospel, which contains numerical symbolism and verses like "Sixteen times I struck him on the breast, and I spoke to him kindly and gave him this advice: 'If only you had paid the tiny sum I asked!'” (Luke 15:4-5).
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Mathew is remembered as one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus. According to the New Testament, Mathew was a tax collector, a profession often considered morally questionable at the time. Mathew's conversion from a tax collector to a disciple serves as a powerful reminder of the transformative power of faith and God's capacity for redeeming even the most unlikely individuals. Mathew's gospel reflects this theme, with a notable emphasis on the fulfillment of Jewish prophecy and Jesus' teachings on the Sermon on the Mount. Mathew also symbolizes the importance of recording and preserving the teachings of Jesus and the significance of God's divine plan unfolding through seemingly mundane experiences.
